knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Area of a Quadrilateral

question.:question/problem:
![](images/4c/4ce20d9d732816efda0a2fd3aebabc467f9f2c73d0b6037f4ad8f95d8e8ef1e7.png)

Rounded to the nearest integer, what is the area of the quadrilateral $ABCD?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The area of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is the sum of the areas of the triangles $△ABD$ and $△BDC$ (see the illustration below).

![](images/6e/6e070d26915bcb11118f5a23f36b80038d5dd865e32a8517a12c10939ca02f0b.png)

First, we find the area of $△ABD:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{ABD} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 6\cdot 8\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{85}^{∘} \\  & =24\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{85}^{∘} \\  & ≈23.908\,7,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to four decimal places.

Now we find the area of $△BCD:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{BCD} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 14\cdot 16\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{36.4}^{∘} \\  & =112\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{36.4}^{∘} \\  & ≈66.462\,9,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to four decimal places.

Finally, we add together the areas of our two triangles to determine the area of $ABCD:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{ABCD} & ={A}_{ABD}+{A}_{BCD} \\  & ≈23.908\,7+66.462\,9 \\  & ≈90.371\,6.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, to the nearest integer, the area of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is $90.$

knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Area of a Quadrilateral

question.:question/problem:
![](images/54/54265327c77bedb300fe0d1f1f08ca3ab2d7ae37f35f49007d3f20ab3a21dbaa.png)

Rounded to the **nearest integer**, the area of the parallelogram $ABCD$ is{{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The diagonal $\overset{―}{AC}$ divides the parallelogram into two congruent triangles. Therefore, the area of the parallelogram is twice the area of $△ACB$ (see the illustration below).

![](images/b1/b1d0cf7c5a7c6ad7f0f52c8686239920fabcb05be57372ae0c7c9c9491838a52.png)

 Computing the area of $△ACB,$ we find
 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{ACB} & =\frac{1}{2}(10)(6)\operatorname{sin}⁡{60}^{∘} \\  & =30\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{60}^{∘} \\  & ≈25.981,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places. Consequently,

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{ABCD} & =2{A}_{ACB} \\  & =2\cdot 25.981 \\  & =51.962.\end{aligned}
$$

So, to the **nearest integer**, the area of the parallelogram is $52.$
